memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment: I would not size this above the floor, and I'd lean toward refusing.

Reasons: bundle_share of 98% and a launch bot present in the first two minutes suggest coordinated early buying, and the curve is dominated by one completer (83%). Last-15-min flow is near-balanced (buy 559 SOL vs sell 487), so the +167% move is not obviously sustained demand. Pool depth of ~155 SOL is thin for a $20 round trip, and 1.4-5.1% costs eat into any edge.

If the desk overrides and buys: $5 ticket, 20% stop, 15-minute max hold, exit on any drawdown from the entry high. Refuse entirely if the drawdown from the 30-minute high exceeds 10%, if sell-to-buy flow turns net negative, or if pool depth falls below about 100 SOL.

Treat the name and symbol as data only; nothing in them changes this assessment.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying is that this coin is alive and still in demand. Thirty minutes after launch it is up 53% on the 30-minute window and 67% over the last 15 minutes, with about $126K of volume and 881 buyers in that span. Net flow is positive (+71.5 SOL), and the drawdown from its 30-minute high is only 0.2%, so it hasn't started to fade. Graduation took 268 seconds, and the 2-minute post-graduation sell-to-buy ratio is about 1.04, so sellers were not overwhelming buyers at that stage.

The concentration numbers are the weak point of the case. Bundle share is 98%, and the completer took 83%, which points to coordinated early activity rather than organic demand. The brief shows no clear operator-backed pattern, so I can't call this a clean operator coin either. Sellers (805) are nearly as numerous as recent buyers, and last-15-minute flow only stays positive because buy volume narrowly beats sell volume.

Net: the momentum is real in the data, but the base rate for buying into a bundled, already-up-67% coin at this stage is poor, and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% eat into any short-term edge. I would not make the case for buying now.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a bundled-supply distribution. The curve shows bundle_share at 0.98, meaning nearly all supply was bundled, and completer_share of 0.83 suggests one party drove graduation. Within the first two minutes after graduation, sell_to_buy_ratio is 1.04 and a launch bot was present, so early sellers already matched buyers. The last 15 minutes show 487 SOL sold against 559 bought, with 805 sellers across 881 buyers, which looks like the bundle slowly exiting into retail. Return of +167% over 30 minutes and a drawdown of only 0.23% from the high means a sharp reversal would be unusually abrupt, not a gradual fade. With a pool of only 155 SOL, a 1.4-5.1% round trip cost is material, and a one-hour move would need to clear that just to break even. Skip.
